newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt awards airport contract to Kuwait's Kharafi.
newsitem.headline: Egypt awards airport contract to Kuwait's Kharafi.

text.p: Egypt has awarded a Kuwaiti firm a contract to build, operate and transfer (BOT) an airport at a cost of 120 million pounds ($35.4 million), Transport and Communications Minister Soleiman Metwalli said on Wednesday.
Mohamed Abdulmuhsin Kharafi and Sons will build the airport at Marsa Alam on the Red Sea in three to four years and operate it for 40 years, the minister said in a statement faxed to Reuters.

The project includes the construction of a main runway and an auxiliary one, a control tower, a passenger terminal and other commercial facilities, such as restaurants, a cargo terminal and duty-free shops.
The contract, the first of its kind in Egypt under its privatisation-led economic reform programme, has still to be finally approved by the cabinet, the statement said.
The Civil Aviation Authority is in final negotiations with a Saudi firm to build an airport at the Red Sea resort of Dahab, also on a BOT basis, it added.
Airports at Bahariya and Farafra oases in the Western Desert and at El Alamein on the Mediterranean coast were re-offered to investors, it said.
Egypt has also offered private investors BOT roads and is considering drafting private investors to set up power stations under the same formula.
